                                                                                    Minden, NV 89423


 The Board of County Commissioners sit jointly as the following boards: Liquor Board, License Board,
 Tahoe-Douglas Transportation District Board, Water District Board, and the Redevelopment Agency.
 Agenda items may be taken out of order, may be combined for consideration, or may be removed from
 the agenda at any time. All items designated “for possible action” may include discussion by the
 County Commissioners and they may take action to approve, modify, deny, take “no action,” or
 continue the item.

 To Watch the Meeting: Members of the public may click on the following link to watch the livestream
 of the Board of County Commissioners meeting: https://www.youtube.com/@douglascountynevada

 Written Public Comment: To offer public comment before the Board meeting, members of the public
 may submit public comments online through the County’s public comment form by clicking on the
 following link:
 https://www.douglascountynv.gov/government/board_of_county_commissioners/public_comment

 Public Comment During the Meeting: Members of the public may attend the meeting in person at the
 address listed at the top of the agenda to provide public comment.

 Supporting Materials:
 Copies of supporting material can be requested in person from the Douglas County Clerk/Treasurer's
 Office, 1616 8th Street, Minden, Nevada or by calling Nicki Leeper at 775-782-9014. Electronic copies
 of the agenda and supporting materials are also available at the following websites:

 State of Nevada Public Notices Website: https://notice.nv.gov/
 Douglas County Meeting website: https://douglascountynv.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?
 view_id=1

 Notice to Persons with Disabilities:
 Members of the public who are disabled or require special assistance or accommodations are requested
 to notify the Douglas County Manager's Office in writing at Post Office Box 218, Minden, Nevada
 89423 or by calling 775-782-9821 at least 20 hours in advance of the meeting.

 Members of the public may call the County Manager’s office at 775-782-9821 to obtain help
 making public comment using any of the foregoing methods.

 A copy of the finalized agenda is posted at the Minden Inn at 1594 Esmeralda Avenue, Minden
 Nevada.




Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                              May 21, 2026
                                                                                                     1

DOUGLAS COUNTY BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS

                                           FINAL AGENDA
                                              May 21, 2026

 LUNCH BREAK
 The Board of County Commissioners may break for lunch at approximately noon and will
 reconvene after a break at the discretion of the Chairperson.

 1.   CALL TO ORDER

 2.   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
      Led by Commissioner Danny Tarkanian

 3.   PUBLIC COMMENT (No Action)
      Forum Restrictions and Orderly Conduct of Business
      The Board of County Commissioners conducts the business of Douglas County and its citizens
      during its meetings. The Board may impose reasonable, content-neutral restrictions on public
      comment such as comments that are on topics that are not within the jurisdiction, authority, or
      control of the Board of County Commissioners, or if the content of the comment is willfully
      disruptive of the meeting by being irrelevant, repetitious, slanderous, offensive, inflammatory,
      irrational, or amounts to a personal attack or interfering with the rights of other speakers. The
      presiding officer may order the removal of any person whose statement or other conduct disrupts
      the orderly, efficient or safe conduct of the meeting. Warnings against disruptive comments or
      behavior may or may not be given prior to removal. Hand clapping, making remarks or gestures
      from the audience that may interrupt, interfere or prevent any speaker from commenting should
      not occur.

      Responses to Public Comments
      The Board of County Commissioners can deliberate or take action only if a matter has been listed
      on an agenda properly posted prior to the meeting. During the public comment period, speakers
      may address matters listed or not listed on the published agenda as long as those matters are within
      the jurisdiction and control of the Board of County Commissioners. The Open Meeting Law does
      not expressly prohibit responses to public comments by the Commissioners. However, responses
      from Commissioners to unlisted public comment topics could become deliberation on a matter
      without notice to the public. On the advice of legal counsel, and to ensure the public has notice of
      all matters the Board of County Commissioners will consider, Commissioners may choose not to
      respond to public comments, except to correct factual inaccuracies, ask clarifying questions, or to
      ask that a matter be listed on a future agenda.

      Public comment is limited to three minutes per speaker unless additional time is granted by the
      Board Chairperson. The Board of Commissioners uses timing lights to ensure that everyone has
      an opportunity to speak. You will see a green light when you begin, and then a yellow light which
      indicates that you have thirty seconds left and should conclude your comments. Once the light
      turns red, please sit down.

      In addition to opening public comment, public comment will also be taken on administrative
      agenda items that are identified for possible action and closing public comment. If you plan to
      speak on a specific agenda item that is on the administrative agenda and identified for possible
Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                                 May 21, 2026
                                                                                                        2

action, then please provide your public comment when that agenda item is heard. Public
      comment will not be taken on Liquor Board agenda items. If you would like to provide public
      comment on Liquor Board agenda items, please provide your public comment during opening
      public comment or closing public comment.

      Public comment must be limited to matters that are within the jurisdiction and control of the
      Board of County Commissioners. Public comment must be addressed to the Chairperson and not
      to members of the public so that the Board may take future action on the issues that are raised by
      the public.

      At this time, public comment will be taken on those items that are within the jurisdiction and
      control of the Board of County Commissioners.

 4.   APPROVAL OF AGENDA
      For possible action. Approval of the proposed agenda. The Board of Commissioners reserves the
      right to take items in a different order to accomplish business in the most efficient manner, to
      combine two or more agenda items for consideration, and to remove items from the agenda or
      delay discussion relating to items on the agenda.

 5.   RECESS AS THE BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS CONVENE AS THE
      BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS SITTING JOINTLY WITH THE REGIONAL
      TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION

 REGIONAL TRANSPORATION COMMISSION AGENDA

      6.1 For possible action. Discussion to approve the draft minutes of the July 18, 2025, Regional
          Transportation Commission meeting. (Philip Ritger, Director Public Works)

      6.2 For possible action. Discussion to elect a Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson for the Regional
          Transportation Commission for a term ending December 31, 2026. (Philip Ritger, Public
          Works Director)

 JOINT MEETING ADMINISTRATIVE AGENDA

      7.   For possible action. Discussion to direct staff to either proceed with or p ause construction of
           Muller Parkway Phase 2, Improvements PWP# DO 2024-227, pending resolution of the
           Muller Parkway litigation; and for staff to issue a change order to remove Phase 2 from the
           scope of work under the current contract with Qualcon Contractors, Inc., at this time based
           on the County's inability to proceed with construction. (Jeremy Hutchings, County Engineer,
           and AJ Hames, Deputy District Attorney)

 8.   ADJOURN AS BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS SITTING JOINTLY WITH
      THE REGIONAL TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION AND RECONVENE AS BOARD
      OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS

 APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MINUTES

      9.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the draft minutes of the regular meeting of April
           16, 2026, of the Board of County Commissioners.


Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                                  May 21, 2026
                                                                                                         3

CONSENT CALENDAR
 Items appearing on the Consent Calendar are items that can be adopted with one motion unless an item
 is pulled by a Commissioner or a member of the public. Members of the public who wish to have a
 consent item placed on the Administrative Agenda shall make that request during the public comment
 section at the beginning of the meeting and specifically state why they are making the request. If items
 are pulled for discussion by a vote of the Board of County Commissioners, they will automatically be
 placed on the Administrative Agenda to be heard at the discretion of the Chairperson or may be
 continued until another meeting.

 10. CONSENT ITEMS

      A.   For possible action. Discussion to approve Task Order "E," in the amount of $109,030, to the
           professional services agreement with Lochner (formerly "Armstrong Consultants Inc.") for
           engineering services at the Minden-Tahoe Airport, and authorize the County Manager or
           Public Works Director to execute the task order and any required documents. The Task Order
           includes the design through construction of the pavement rehabilitation of the P-51 Court
           Taxilanes in the northwest area of the airport (Airport Improvement Plan number 3-32-0013-
           XXX-2026). (Heather MacDonnell, Airport Manager)

      B.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a federal grant application for an award of up to
           $183,397 for the rehabilitation of the P-51 Taxilane at Minden Tahoe Airport and authorize
           the Director of Public Works to sign all related documents. The total County contribution
           will be $9,653. (Heather MacDonnell, Airport Manager)

      C.   For possible action. Discussion on the Outdoor Festival License application submitted by
           Mike Frates of the Golden Nugget Lake Tahoe Hotel & Casino for the Golden Nugget 4th of
           July Party to be held Saturday, July 4, 2026, from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM, at the Golden
           Nugget Lake Tahoe Hotel & Casino, 50 Highway 50, Stateline, Nevada. (Amy Burgans,
           Clerk-Treasurer)

      D.   For possible action. Discussion on the Outdoor Festival License application submitted by
           Jody Brunz, Town of Genoa Manager, for Genoa's 107th Annual Candy Dance Craft Faire to
           be held September 26, 2026, from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM, and September 27, 2026, from 7:00
           AM to 8:00 PM, to be held throughout the Town of Genoa, Nevada. (Amy Burgans, Clerk-
           Treasurer)

      E.   For possible action. Discussion and review of the Douglas County Treasurer's Monthly
           Statement for March 2026 submitted per Nevada Revised Statutes 354.280(2). (Amy
           Burgans, Clerk-Treasurer)

      F.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the Third Amendment to a Contract for
           Professional Services by an Independent Contractor between Wood Rodgers, Inc. and
           Douglas County to extend the contract term from June 30, 2026, to December 31, 2026, and
           increase the contract by $9,640, and up to a 10% increase if needed, and authorize the County
           Manager to sign any required docuements related to the Transfer Development Rights (TDR)
           Study. (Kate O'Neil, Principal Planner)

      G.   For possible action. Discussion to accept a $4,000 donation from the Rotary Club of Minden
           to the Community Services Department to be used for improvements at the Herbig Park
           Pickleball Complex; and adopt Resolution 2026R-024, which augments the budget in the

Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                                May 21, 2026
                                                                                                       4

Room Tax fund in the amount of the donation. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

     H.   For possible action. Discussion to accept a donation of $12,000 from the Sierra Sagebrush
          Flyers to the Community Services Department to be used for improvements at the Model
          Airplane Complex; and adopt Resolution 2026R-026, which augments the budget in the
          Room Tax fund in the amount of the donation. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

     I.   For possible action. Discussion to approve an amendment to the contract between Douglas
          County and Minden Lawyers LLC to provide legal services to the Douglas County Public
          Guardian and Public Administrator, increasing the total amount of allowable hourly services
          from $50,000 to $70,000, and authorize the County Manager to sign any required
          documents. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

     J.   For possible action. Discussion to increase the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Purchase Order with
          Capitol Reporters from $129,545 to $192,726 for court reporter services for all Douglas
          County courts. (Delores Goelz, Judicial Fiscal Management Analyst)

     K.   For possible action. Discussion to accept a $24,888 Nutritional Services Incentive Program
          (NSIP) grant award from the Nevada Aging and Disability Services Division (ADSD), for the
          time period of October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026, and authorize the County
          Manager to sign the grant award. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

     L.   For possible action. Discussion to: (1) accept the Business Impact Statement prepared
          pursuant to NRS 237.080 for Resolution 2026R-011 , which will update the Douglas County
          Animal Services Operations Manual, pertaining to Title 6, including adding or increasing
          existing Animal Services fees; (2) find that Resolution 2026R-011 is not likely to impose a
          direct and significant economic burden upon a business, or directly restrict the formation,
          operation or expansion of business; and (3) approve the objection process set forth therein for
          any aggrieved business to object to Resolution 2026R-011. (Brook Adie, Community
          Services Director, and AJ Hames, Deputy District Attorney)

     M. For possible action. Discussion to approve Fiscal Year 2025-26 budget transfers totaling
        $140,500 for various funds. (Kathy Lewis, Chief Operating Officer)

     N.   For possible action. Discussion to adopt Resolution 2026R-027, a resolution augmenting the
          2025-26 Fiscal Year Douglas County Water Utility Fund (328) budget by increasing overall
          expenditure authority by $78,168. (Kathy Lewis, Chief Operating Officer)

     O.   For possible action. Discussion to adopt Resolution 2026R-028, a resolution augmenting
          various funds for the Fiscal Year 2025-26 budget to recognize actual opening fund balances
          and increase expenditure authority by $12,733,602 for unanticipated expenditures and
          operational requirements identified during the fiscal year of $1,911,130, with any
          unappropriated balances remaining in fund reserves of $10,822,472. (Kathy Lewis, Chief
          Operating Officer)

     P.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the auditor's report on Douglas County's general
          ledger cash balances through April 15, 2026, per Nevada Revised Statute 251.030. (Kathy
          Lewis, Chief Operating Officer)

     Q.   For possible action. Discussion to award a $99,500 construction contract to Haen
          Constructors for the Cave Rock/Skyland Fire Hydrant Replacement Project and authorize the
Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                                May 21, 2026
                                                                                                       5

Director of Public Works to execute the contract. (Rick Robillard, Deputy Public Works
           Director)

      R.   For possible action. Discussion on the possible acceptance of the highest bid obtained from
           the public internet auction held on Tuesday, May 19, 2026, to sell a 1-acre parcel owned by
           Douglas County (APN 1022-17-002-010). In accordance with Resolution 2026R-019 and
           NRS 244.282, the County Commissioners can either (1) accept the highest bid or (2) reject
           any and all bids and withdraw the real property from sale if it deems that action to be for the
           best public interest. (Philip Ritger, Public Works Director)

      S.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the Douglas County Sheriff's Office Quarterly Jail
           Division Status Report for the First Quarter of January to March, 2026. (Captain Stanley)

 ADMINISTRATIVE AGENDA
 The Chairperson will read the agenda title into the public record and will have the discretion to
 determine how the item will be presented. Agenda items may be considered ahead of or after the
 schedule indicated by this agenda. Public comment will be taken on items that are identified for possible
 action.

 11. ITEM(S) PULLED FROM THE CONSENT AGENDA WILL BE HEARD AT THIS TIME

 COMMUNITY SERVICES

      12. For possible action. Presentation of the proposed WALLS Mural Project to be located at the
          Douglas County Community Arts Center, and discussion to approve the mural rendering
          concept for the Project pending approval of a Special Use Permit by the Douglas County
          Planning Commission, and to authorize the Community Services Director to enter into all
          necessary agreements for the Project at no cost to Douglas County. (Brook Adie, Community
          Services Director)

 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

      13.1 For possible action. Discussion on Major Modification Application DP25-0210, modifying
           the development schedule for the Ashland Park Planned Development (DP20-0219 and
           DP20-0220). This modification changes the completion dates for final maps of Phases 1
           through 5. The subject site is located in the Gardnerville Community Plan at 1424 Toler
           Lane, on the north side of Toler Lane between Harvest Avenue and Decker Road. The owner
           is Matt Carter, Ashland Park LLC, and the applicant's representative is Rob Anderson of
           Wilson Engineers, LLC. (APN 1320-34-002-054). (Kate O'Neil, Principal Planner)

      13.2 For possible action. Discussion regarding the 2026 5-Year Capital Improvement Project
           (CIP) Plan Update to the 2024 Douglas County Stormwater Master Plan. (Courtney Walker,
           Stormwater Program Manager)

      13.3 For possible action. Discussion to amend the 2024 Douglas County Stormwater Master Plan
           by updating Appendix B: Douglas County Stormwater Operations and Maintenance Manual.
           (Courtney Walker, Stormwater Program Manager)

      13.4 For possible action. Discussion to adopt the Douglas County Stormwater Utility Critical
           Lands Conservation, Acquisition, and Management Plan and direct staff to incorporate the

Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                                 May 21, 2026
                                                                                                        6

plan into the Douglas County Stormwater Master Plan as Appendix E. (Jenifer Davidson,
          County Manager)

 COUNTY MANAGER

     14. For presentation only. Announcements/reports/updates from County Commission members,
         including updates on the various boards and/or commissions that they may be a member of or
         a liaison to, or any other meetings/functions they have attended, and any request by a
         Commissioner for discussion of a future agenda item. (Chairman Gardner)

 15. CLOSING PUBLIC COMMENT (No Action)
     At this time, public comment will be taken on those items that are within the jurisdiction and
     control of the Board of Commissioners or those agenda items where public comment has not
     already been taken.

 16. ADJOURNMENT
